title: Turkmenistan
capsule: The Republic of Turkmenistan declared independence on October 27, 1991, following the dissolution of the Soviet Union, and adopted a permanent neutrality status recognized by the United Nations in 1995. Under President Saparmurat Niyazov (Türkmenbaşy, 'Head of all Turkmens'), who ruled until his death in December 2006, the state developed an extreme personality cult while maintaining an isolationist, hydrocarbon-dependent economy centered on vast natural gas reserves. Gurbanguly Berdimuhamedow succeeded Niyazov in 2007 and oversaw modest liberalization of the personality cult while retaining authoritarian governance; he transferred formal presidential power to his son Serdar Berdimuhamedow in 2022.
